items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I remember that Bird came and sat in with us at Tony Scott’s combo at Cafe Society

ctx.x: 1952. So we added a drummer to the duo, who was Charlie Smith, and the bass player was a sub that day actually, he was Sandy Block. And sure enough, Bird and Dizzy came on the show and they did “Hot House” and that turned out to be the only sound film that exists of Charlie Parker. And it’s also a very young Dizzy at that point if you look, if you see him. I worked a little bit with Dizzy later on in one thing or another and I remember that Bird came and sat in with us at Tony Scott’s combo at Cafe Society and I…
Most of them are, one way or another.

items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: They cut out the piano solo and they didn’t say who was in the band. In fact I was there slightly to the left of Parker

ctx.x: Yeah. Well of course you make it in almost all those things because of your participation in, it was the only clip of Charlie Parker, right?

Oh well yeah. I wasn’t very pleased that they cut out my piano solo. They cut out the piano solo and they didn’t say who was in the band. In fact I was there slightly to the left of Parker, as I say if you didn’t blink then you could see the side of my head for about one and a half seconds.
That’s pretty amazing that’s the only piece.
